::: {.why}
The order in which coefficients survive as the penalty rises is a ranking you get for free, and comparing it against your standalone signal ranking tells you which signals are carrying independent information.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Interpret a regularization path in terms of which features carry independent information.
- Report the disagreement between the path ordering and the standalone ranking, and explain the largest discrepancy.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Compare the two rankings side by side: the order features survive in the path, and their standalone net information ratios from day 181. Then explain the largest discrepancy, which will be a signal with a good standalone result that drops early because it is nearly a combination of two others.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Check the stability of the path, which is where most feature ranking claims fall apart: refit on bootstrap resamples of the training set and report how often each feature is in the top three. A ranking that is not stable across resamples is not a ranking.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Record the selection-frequency table into reports/milestone-07-ml.md, since it is more honest than any single ordering.
:::
:::
